claims.text: Conventionally processed CoCrFeNi has relatively coarse grains and no engineered surface gradient.
Severe plastic deformation followed by short-duration annealing near 800 °C will produce an ultra-nanocrystalline gradient surface layer in CoCrFeNi.
Cold-rolling reduction and annealing conditions can control grain size, recrystallization, and precipitate development in a CoCrFeNi-related alloy.
The proposed processing treatment will create a graded surface zone rather than only a bulk ultrafine-grained microstructure.
The processed surface will evolve protective oxidic features during tribological operation.
At lower temperatures, fine grains will provide high hardness and resistance to deformation.
At higher temperatures, controlled oxidation will form a continuous lubricious oxide film on treated CoCrFeNi.
Severe plastic deformation will increase the density of grain boundaries in the treated surface.
The increased grain-boundary density will provide sites for dynamic recrystallization during sliding.
The post-deformation anneal itself will enable controlled oxidation and formation of a thin, adherent lubricious glaze.
A nanocrystalline glaze can reduce adhesive and oxidative wear at high temperature.
A hierarchical or gradient microstructure can progressively accommodate or release frictional stresses during sliding.
The treated CoCrFeNi alloy will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than untreated CoCrFeNi from 25 °C to 800 °C.
The treated CoCrFeNi alloy will have a lower wear rate than untreated CoCrFeNi from 25 °C to 800 °C.
Untreated CoCrFeNi has higher friction and wear that worsens at elevated temperature because of uncontrolled oxidation and coarse grains.
The treatment will remain beneficial in ambient atmosphere under moderate-to-high contact loads and laboratory sliding speeds.
Performance under extreme loads, non-ambient atmospheres, and prolonged high-temperature dwell times is uncertain.
Over-oxidation or nonuniform microstructural evolution could compromise the proposed tribological improvement.
